incumbent.name: James Gallagher
incumbent.note: Won the June 2, 2026 special election (old boundaries) to finish the late Doug LaMalfa's term; running here

candidates.name: James Gallagher
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since June 2026; former California Assembly Republican leader (2022-2025) from Sutter County, attorney and partner in his family's farming operation.
candidates.platform: Says he wants to make life more affordable for North State families through lower taxes, fees and regulation. Calls for tougher laws against crime and for protecting farms and small businesses from what he describes as excessive government regulation.

candidates.name: Mike McGuire
candidates.bio: State senator from the North Coast's 2nd district since 2014 and former president pro tempore of the California State Senate (2024-2025).
candidates.platform: Campaigns on affordability and job growth for working families, wildfire recovery and expanded state firefighting capacity, and protecting rural hospitals, health care access and reproductive rights. Frames the race as standing up to what he calls the Trump administration's cuts to health care and wildfire budgets.

1.likely_winner_basis: All three forecasters rate the redrawn seat Solid/Safe Democratic, and Democratic candidates combined for roughly 57% of the June primary vote (McGuire 41.8% plus Denney 14.2%) against Gallagher's 42.1%.
1.partisan_lean: D+7 (Cook PVI, new district; was R+12 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 54.5%, Trump 42.3%
1.summary: Republican James Gallagher, who won the June special election under the old lines after Doug LaMalfa's death, faces Democratic former Senate leader Mike McGuire in a district Prop 50 flipped on paper from R+12 to D+7. The new map removed Republican-leaning Redding and the Yuba-Sutter area and added Democratic-leaning Santa Rosa and Sonoma County communities, making this one of the five GOP seats the plan targeted. Gallagher narrowly topped the primary, but the two Democrats together outpolled him.

candidates.name: Jared Huffman
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2013 and ranking Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee; former state assemblymember and environmental attorney from San Rafael.
candidates.platform: Prioritizes lowering everyday costs (groceries, energy, health care, housing) and blames tariffs and what he calls tax cuts for the rich for the affordability crisis. Pledges aggressive oversight of the Trump administration, a ban on congressional stock trading and Supreme Court ethics rules, and defense of voting rights, church-state separation and the rule of law; a longtime advocate for climate action.

candidates.name: Robin Littau
candidates.bio: Enterprise Elementary School District board member in Redding, U.S. Coast Guard veteran and owner of two small businesses.
candidates.platform: Says she wants to create, replace and revise 'common sense legislation' that benefits Americans, including reducing what she calls burdensome taxation. Emphasizes her background as a veteran, single mother, school board member and community volunteer, and her Christian faith as the basis of her values.

2.likely_winner_basis: Rated Solid/Safe Democratic by all forecasters; Huffman took 56.5% in the primary to Littau's 11.4%.
2.partisan_lean: D+13 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+24 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 60.7%, Trump 36.1%
2.summary: Seven-term Democrat Jared Huffman faces Republican school board member Robin Littau in the North Coast district running from the Golden Gate to the Oregon border. Prop 50 made the seat noticeably less Democratic (PVI D+24 to D+13) by extending it into interior northern counties formerly in the Republican 1st district, but it remains safely Democratic.

incumbent.name: Ami Bera
incumbent.note: Represents the current 6th district; running in the redrawn 3rd (the old 3rd's incumbent, Kevin Kiley, is running in the new 6th)

candidates.name: Ami Bera
candidates.bio: Physician and U.S. Representative from the Sacramento area since 2013, currently representing the 6th district.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on affordable health care and preventive care, drawing on his career as a doctor. Supports an economy built on competition, job training and clean-energy jobs, and a transition toward sustainable energy and environmental policy.

candidates.name: Robb Tucker
candidates.bio: Nevada County supervisor (since 2025) and former operator of his family's business in the Sierra foothills.
candidates.platform: Describes himself as a solutions-oriented leader focused on public safety, supporting small businesses and job creation, and balancing growth, development and agriculture to protect quality of life. Says he would bring his local-government and executive experience to Washington.

3.likely_winner_basis: All forecasters rate the redrawn seat Solid/Safe Democratic; Bera led the primary 34.3% to 29.9% and Democrats combined for about 56% of the vote.
3.partisan_lean: D+6 (Cook PVI, new district; was R+2 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 53.3%, Trump 43.2%
3.summary: Prop 50 remade the 3rd district by stripping out Republican-leaning Placer County suburbs such as Roseville and Lincoln and adding Democratic-leaning parts of Sacramento and its inner suburbs, shifting it from R+2 to D+6. Incumbent Kevin Kiley opted to run in the new 6th, so Democrat Ami Bera moved over from the 6th to face Republican Nevada County supervisor Robb Tucker.

candidates.name: Mike Thompson
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 1999, former state senator, Vietnam-era Army veteran and Napa Valley vineyard owner.
candidates.platform: Says he is running because costs are skyrocketing and democracy is on the line. Runs on his record on job creation, health care and veterans' issues and on a reputation for bipartisan problem-solving.

candidates.name: Eric Jones
candidates.bio: Yale graduate, former partner at Dragoneer Investment Group and founder of the American Dream Institute and a family foundation.
candidates.platform: Pledges to close corporate loopholes to help working people and small businesses, to refuse corporate PAC and lobbyist money, and never to trade stocks in Congress. Cites his family's reliance on food stamps and Medicaid and his nonprofit work helping veterans and families as shaping his focus on affordability.

4.likely_winner_basis: Fourteen-term incumbent led the all-Democratic primary 41.0% to 22.2%; the seat is Solid/Safe Democratic regardless of winner.
4.partisan_lean: D+8 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+17 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 55.7%, Trump 41.2%
4.summary: Two Democrats advanced: longtime incumbent Mike Thompson and self-funding first-time candidate Eric Jones, after Republicans split roughly 37% of the primary vote among seven candidates. Prop 50 made the North Bay/Yolo seat less Democratic (D+17 to D+8) by absorbing Republican-leaning Sacramento Valley territory from the old 1st and Placer-area suburbs, though it remains safe for the party.

candidates.name: Tom McClintock
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2009 and former 22-year state legislator; chairs the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Federal Lands and sits on the Budget Committee.
candidates.platform: Runs as a fiscal conservative, proposing to curb unauthorized appropriations, control mandatory spending and balance the budget, and opposing new state bonds and spending programs. Advocates building new reservoirs and changing federal land management to promote forest health, public access and fire prevention.

candidates.name: Michael Masuda
candidates.bio: Engineer from Amador County who designed tools for the military and most recently worked at the State Department on science and national-security policy.
candidates.platform: Presents himself as 'an engineer, not a politician' focused on practical solutions and bipartisan cooperation. Says he will represent valley, foothill, mountain and desert communities regardless of party and criticizes the incumbent as absent from the district.

5.likely_winner_basis: Rated Solid/Safe Republican (Decision Desk HQ: Likely R); McClintock won 61.3% of the primary vote.
5.partisan_lean: R+10 (Cook PVI, new district; was R+8 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Trump 59.1%, Harris 38.4%
5.summary: Veteran Republican Tom McClintock faces Democratic engineer Michael Masuda in the Gold Country and Sierra Nevada seat. Prop 50 left this as one of California's few safe Republican districts, making it slightly more Republican (R+8 to R+10) as the map concentrated GOP voters here.

incumbent.name: Kevin Kiley
incumbent.note: Represents the current 3rd district; elected as a Republican in 2024, now independent (No Party Preference) and running in the redrawn 6th

candidates.name: Kevin Kiley
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2023 and former state assemblymember from Roseville; a former teacher and deputy attorney general who left the Republican Party and is on the ballot with no party preference.
candidates.platform: Runs as an independent emphasizing bipartisan work on affordability, citing bills on gas taxes, Social Security fairness, Medicare protection and AI safety, plus federal grants for Highway 65/I-80 and Lake Tahoe restoration. Stresses accessibility through town-hall 'conversations' across the district.

candidates.name: Richard Pan
candidates.bio: Pediatrician and former state senator (2014-2022) from Sacramento, known for authoring California's school vaccine laws; ran for Sacramento mayor in 2024.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on protecting the Affordable Care Act and Medicare, lowering prescription drug and insulin costs, and defending what he calls science-based public health policy against HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Pledges to hold the Trump administration accountable and to follow evidence in federal health and environmental policy.

polls.pollster: The Bullfinch Group (for Independent Leadership Council, pro-Kiley)

6.likely_winner_basis: Forecasters favor the Democrat (Cook Solid D, Sabato Likely D, Inside Elections Lean D) in a Harris+8 seat, though the two public polls show a tie and a 4-point Pan lead with about a quarter undecided.
6.partisan_lean: D+5 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+8 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 52.6%, Trump 44.2%
6.summary: Incumbent Kevin Kiley, whose Placer County base was split up by Prop 50, left the GOP and is running as an independent in the redrawn Sacramento-area 6th, which absorbed Republican-leaning suburbs from his old district (PVI D+8 to D+5). He faces Democrat Richard Pan, a former state senator, after a crowded primary in which Kiley edged Pan 24.3% to 23.2% and a Republican took 20%. Polls are close and this is one of the most competitive House seats in Northern California.

candidates.name: Doris Matsui
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for Sacramento since 2005; former Clinton White House staffer, born in a Japanese American internment camp.
candidates.platform: Runs on experience and relationships in Washington, citing more than $3 billion secured for Sacramento flood protection, work on the Affordable Care Act and transit funding. Frames the defense of democracy through her family's internment history and pledges a government that works for everyone, not the powerful.

candidates.name: Mai Vang
candidates.bio: Sacramento City Council member since 2020, former school board member and Sacramento State lecturer; daughter of Hmong refugees and eldest of 16 children.
candidates.platform: Progressive platform: ban congressional stock trading and lobbyist gifts, end dark-money super PACs, and pass Medicare for All while taking on insurers and drug companies. Takes no corporate PAC or AIPAC money and cites her council record creating a Children's Fund and saving libraries.

polls.pollster: Data for Progress (for Justice Democrats, Leaders We Deserve, Working Families Party, pro-Vang)

7.likely_winner_basis: Genuinely uncertain: challenger Vang led the primary 31.2% to 29.1% and the only public (Vang-aligned) poll 32-28 with 40% undecided, but the incumbent may consolidate the roughly 37% of primary voters who backed eliminated Republicans.
7.partisan_lean: D+7 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+16 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 54.8%, Trump 42.0%
7.summary: Two Democrats face off in Sacramento: 11-term incumbent Doris Matsui and Sacramento councilmember Mai Vang, who narrowly topped the primary with backing from Justice Democrats. Prop 50 made the district considerably less Democratic (D+16 to D+7) by redistributing Sacramento-area Democratic voters to shore up the neighboring 3rd and 6th, so the eliminated Republican electorate is unusually large for an intraparty contest.

candidates.name: John Garamendi
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2009; former California lieutenant governor, insurance commissioner, state legislator and deputy interior secretary.
candidates.platform: Champions 'Make It In America' policies to rebuild domestic manufacturing and Buy America rules, opposes the Delta tunnels and backs water-infrastructure investment. Emphasizes health care access in underserved communities, veterans' benefits and protecting the missions at Travis and Beale Air Force bases.

candidates.name: Rudy Recile
candidates.bio: Retired U.S. Army major with 26 years of service, former USDA employee and small business owner from Fairfield; the district's Republican nominee in 2022 and 2024.
candidates.platform: Says public service should be rooted in accountability, transparency and results, and that Washington has stopped listening to families facing rising costs and small businesses facing obstacles. Cites Pentagon and Capitol Hill experience in navigating government to deliver results.

8.likely_winner_basis: Rated Solid/Safe Democratic; Garamendi won 54.4% of the primary and beat Recile comfortably in 2022 and 2024.
8.partisan_lean: D+19 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+24 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 65.5%, Trump 31.4%
8.summary: Democrat John Garamendi faces Republican Rudy Recile for the third straight cycle in the Solano/Contra Costa seat anchored by Vallejo, Fairfield and Richmond. Prop 50 trimmed the district's Democratic margin (D+24 to D+19) as it shifted voters to neighboring targeted districts, but it remains safely Democratic.

candidates.name: Josh Harder
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2019 (for the 9th since 2023), a former venture capitalist and business school instructor from Tracy.
candidates.platform: Focuses on lowering the cost of gas, housing and health care and bringing more doctors to the Valley, along with fighting homelessness and keeping neighborhoods safe. Presents himself as a pragmatic new-generation leader working with farmers, unions and law enforcement.

candidates.name: John McBride
candidates.bio: Longtime strength and conditioning coach at the University of the Pacific and St. Mary's High School in Stockton; ran for this seat in 2024.
candidates.platform: Calls for American energy independence including expanded nuclear power, protecting farmers and the food supply from regulation and low-quality imports, and parental rights including medical freedom in raising children.

9.likely_winner_basis: All forecasters rate the redrawn seat Solid/Safe Democratic (up from Lean D before Prop 50); Harder took 60.8% in the primary.
9.partisan_lean: D+8 (Cook PVI, new district; was D+1 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 54.1%, Trump 42.7%
9.summary: Josh Harder, who won a tight race in 2024, now runs in a much safer San Joaquin County seat after Prop 50 moved it from D+1 to D+8 and shifted Stockton into the neighboring 13th. His Republican opponent is coach John McBride; former Stockton mayor Kevin Lincoln, Harder's 2024 opponent, switched to the 13th. Forecasters moved the race from Lean to Solid Democratic after the new map.

candidates.name: Mark DeSaulnier
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2015 from Concord; former state senator, assemblymember and Contra Costa County supervisor.
candidates.platform: Progressive platform centered on transportation and shorter commutes, workers' rights, education access, lowering inflation and health care costs, expanding affordable housing and protecting democracy. Highlights protecting workers as AI and automation reshape the economy.

candidates.name: Jeff Frese
candidates.bio: Moraga businessman who founded and sold the snack brand Fat Snax, now runs a skincare company, and formerly held product roles at CNN, Nickelodeon and MTV.
candidates.platform: Runs on 'fixing Congress' with eight-year term limits, a congressional stock-trading ban and no-budget-no-pay rules. Calls for ending deficit spending, cutting building red tape, barring Wall Street from buying single-family homes, backing police and ending cashless bail; takes no special-interest money.

10.likely_winner_basis: Rated Solid/Safe Democratic; DeSaulnier won 59.7% of the primary to Frese's 12.9%.
10.partisan_lean: D+18 (Cook PVI, new district; unchanged from the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 65.1%, Trump 31.6%
10.summary: Six-term Democrat Mark DeSaulnier faces first-time Republican candidate Jeff Frese in the Contra Costa County seat covering Concord, Walnut Creek, Danville and San Ramon. Prop 50 left the district's partisan makeup essentially unchanged at D+18, and it remains safely Democratic.

candidates.name: Scott Wiener
candidates.bio: State senator for San Francisco since 2016 and former city supervisor; Harvard-trained attorney known for housing and transit legislation.
candidates.platform: Says he is running to defend San Francisco's values and the Constitution against the Trump administration. Runs on his legislative record holding insurers accountable, protecting LGBTQ youth and families, and banning masked ICE agents, and has long championed housing production.

candidates.name: Connie Chan
candidates.bio: San Francisco supervisor for District 1 since 2021 and budget chair of the Board of Supervisors; first-generation immigrant who grew up in Chinatown.
candidates.platform: Pledges to fight Trump tariffs and cuts, pass Medicare for All, restore Medicare, Medi-Cal and reproductive health funding, and get ICE out of immigrant communities while protecting sanctuary status. Also calls for fully funding public schools, free community college and eliminating student debt.

polls.pollster: Tavern Research (for Jobs And Democracy PAC, pro-Wiener)

11.likely_winner_basis: Wiener led the primary 40.7% to 29.7% and leads both general-election polls (by 11 in a pro-Wiener poll and by 5 in a Chan-campaign poll).
11.partisan_lean: D+36 (Cook PVI, new district; unchanged from the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 81.8%, Trump 14.1%
11.summary: With Nancy Pelosi retiring after nearly four decades, two Democrats compete for the San Francisco seat: state Sen. Scott Wiener, backed by former Mayor London Breed, and Supervisor Connie Chan, endorsed by Pelosi. Prop 50 left this overwhelmingly Democratic city district essentially unchanged (D+36); the contest is between Wiener's housing-focused, party-endorsed coalition and Chan's rival coalition.

candidates.name: Lateefah Simon
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2025, former BART board president and civil rights advocate; vice chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the first blind member of Congress.
candidates.platform: Progressive platform centered on civil rights and social justice; cites three bipartisan small-business bills passed in the House and more than $11 million secured for public safety and transit in the East Bay. Serves on the Oversight and Small Business committees.

candidates.name: Jamie Joyce
candidates.bio: Berkeley-based technology executive and researcher who has led AI teams and built policy tools for governments.
candidates.platform: Centers her campaign on a self-drafted 'MAD Act' covering dark-money disclosure, surveillance limits, AI guardrails and accountability for the Epstein network. Proposes organizing a bloc of members to withhold votes from legislation that does not serve voters and using technology to modernize Congress.

12.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 84.2% of the primary vote against the only other candidate; the seat is Solid/Safe Democratic.
12.partisan_lean: D+39 (Cook PVI, new district; unchanged from the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 84.5%, Trump 10.6%
12.summary: Freshman Democrat Lateefah Simon faces fellow Democrat Jamie Joyce, a technology researcher, in a rematch of the two-candidate primary for the Oakland-Berkeley seat. Prop 50 left the district's lines effectively unchanged (D+39), and no Republican qualified for the ballot.

candidates.name: Adam Gray
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2025 after winning by 187 votes in 2024; former 10-year state assemblymember from Merced, professor and small business owner.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes a bipartisan record and Valley-first independence from party orthodoxy, pointing to telehealth and geothermal work with Republicans. Agenda: lower food, housing and utility costs, more water for families and farms, less red tape for infrastructure, and affordable health care.

candidates.name: Kevin Lincoln
candidates.bio: Former mayor of Stockton (2021-2024), U.S. Marine Corps veteran, pastor and security-company executive; lost the 2024 race for the 9th district 51.8%-48.2%.
candidates.platform: Says Washington's partisanship has done little about the cost of groceries, gas and housing and promises to put people before politics. Cites his mayoral record on jobs, balanced budgets and reductions in crime and homelessness; supports tax cuts and spending reductions, more law-enforcement funding, stricter immigration enforcement and light regulation of AI.

13.likely_winner_basis: Forecasters rate the seat Lean D (Cook), Likely D (Sabato, moved from Lean on Oct. 20) and Tilt D (Inside Elections), and Democrats combined for about 57% of the primary vote, though the GOP's Congressional Leadership Fund had spent $4.34 million here by Oct. 11.
13.partisan_lean: D+2 (Cook PVI, new district; was R+1 under the 2023-2026 map); 2024 presidential: Harris 48.8%, Trump 48.4%
13.summary: Democrat Adam Gray, who won the nation's closest 2024 House race, faces former Stockton mayor Kevin Lincoln in a Central Valley seat that Prop 50 helped by adding Stockton, moving it from R+1 to D+2 (Inside Elections' baseline from even to D+6). Forecasters shifted the race from Toss-up to Lean/Tilt Democratic after the new map (Sabato's Crystal Ball moved it to Likely Democratic on Oct. 20), but heavy Republican outside spending keeps it one of the state's most competitive districts.

incumbent.name: Aisha Wahab
incumbent.note: running here; won the Aug 18, 2026 special-election runoff to replace Eric Swalwell, who resigned Apr 14, 2026, and took office Sep 2, 2026

candidates.name: Aisha Wahab
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since September 2026 after winning the special election; previously a California state senator (2022-2026) and Hayward city councilmember, and the first Afghan American in Congress.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes lowering the cost of housing, health care, child care and utilities, and expanding affordable housing and renter protections. Pledges to defend democracy, women's and civil rights and immigrant families while backing 'victim-first' public safety, and to take on billionaires, 'corporate price-gougers' and Wall Street landlords.

candidates.name: Melissa Hernandez
candidates.bio: President of the BART board of directors and former mayor of Dublin; daughter of migrant farmworkers.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on lowering costs for East Bay families, building affordable housing and protecting health care access. Cites a record as mayor of fiscal responsibility without tax increases while expanding housing and public safety; issue pages also cover childcare, immigration, climate change and emerging technology.

polls.pollster: David Binder Research (pre-primary poll, all candidates)

14.likely_winner_basis: Wahab is the sitting incumbent (via the 2026 special election), led the June primary 38.3% to 17.2%, and has the California Democratic Party and Gov. Newsom's endorsement in a Democrat-vs-Democrat race.
14.partisan_lean: D+19 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 65.4%, Trump 30.6%
14.summary: An all-Democratic general election between Rep. Aisha Wahab, who won the special election to replace Eric Swalwell after his April 2026 resignation, and BART board president Melissa Hernandez. The East Bay seat (Hayward, Fremont, Dublin, Livermore, Pleasanton, Union City) is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+19 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Kevin Mullin
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2023, serving on the Energy and Commerce Committee; previously Speaker pro tempore of the California State Assembly for nearly a decade.
candidates.platform: Prioritizes protecting democracy and voting rights (cosponsor of the Freedom to Vote Act), climate action including the Green New Deal and rail electrification, and lowering housing costs via his Empty Lots to Housing Act. Opposes the 2025 Republican budget's cuts to safety-net programs and the Trump administration's immigration enforcement tactics.

candidates.name: Charles Hoelter
candidates.bio: Retired UPS training supervisor of 25-plus years and longtime San Mateo County resident.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on barring transgender women from women's sports, term limits for politicians, and voter ID with cleanup of voter rolls. Also advocates high-school apprenticeship programs nationwide.

15.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings, a D+26 district, and a 65%-18% primary margin.
15.partisan_lean: D+26 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 72.2%, Trump 24.3%
15.summary: Two-term Democrat Kevin Mullin faces Republican Charles Hoelter in a San Mateo County/southeast San Francisco seat that is among the most Democratic in the state. Mullin took 65% in the top-two primary. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+26 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Sam Liccardo
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative elected in 2024; former San Jose mayor, city councilmember, criminal prosecutor and college professor.
candidates.platform: Focuses on cost of living through bipartisan housing-supply legislation, an ACA tax-credit extension and tariff repeal. Highlights opposition to the Trump administration on rule-of-law and immigration-enforcement issues, and calls for fiscal restraint, clean-energy incentives for data centers and workforce programs at community colleges.

candidates.name: Peter Sundin Soule
candidates.bio: Investor running on a 'common sense' platform; endorsed by the California Republican Assembly and Silicon Valley Association of Conservative Republicans.
candidates.platform: Stresses public safety and enforcement of existing laws, reducing regulation and 'wasteful spending' he says strangle California's economy, and long-term fiscal strength for the next generation.

16.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings, D+25 PVI, and a 75.6%-10.8% primary.
16.partisan_lean: D+25 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 72.3%, Trump 24.2%
16.summary: Freshman Democrat Sam Liccardo, who won a Democrat-vs-Democrat contest in 2024, faces Republican investor Peter Soule in the Peninsula/West Valley seat that is one of the wealthiest districts in the nation. Liccardo cleared 75% in the primary. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+25 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Ro Khanna
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2017 serving on the Armed Services and Oversight committees; former attorney, professor and Commerce Department deputy assistant secretary.
candidates.platform: Official issue priorities include spreading Silicon Valley's economic success nationally, expanding health coverage to all Americans, debt-free public college, climate action, housing affordability and homeownership, immigrant-friendly policies, responsible technology governance and congressional reform.

candidates.name: Ritesh Tandon
candidates.bio: Engineer and entrepreneur with 24 years in tech who founded his own company; repeat candidate for this seat and plaintiff in the Supreme Court case Tandon v. Newsom.
candidates.platform: Leads with affordability: more housing through cutting red tape, lower taxes and reduced federal spending. Pledges to ban congressional stock trading (criticizing Khanna's household wealth), hold regular town halls, back police and first responders, and pursue enforcement-focused but pro-legal-immigration reform.

17.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings, D+21 PVI, and a 62%-15% primary margin.
17.partisan_lean: D+21 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 67.3%, Trump 28.3%
17.summary: Five-term Democrat Ro Khanna faces Republican tech executive Ritesh Tandon in a rematch-style contest for the Silicon Valley seat (Fremont, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara, Cupertino, Milpitas). All forecasters rate it Solid/Safe Democratic. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+21 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Zoe Lofgren
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 1995 and chair of the California Democratic congressional delegation, representing San Jose and the Salinas Valley.
candidates.platform: Campaign site centers on reclaiming the House majority and 'fighting for California's values,' citing her record on immigration, health care, technology, transportation and women's issues.

candidates.name: Shane Lewis
candidates.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran and R&D electrical test engineer at a medical-device company; former church worship leader and small-business owner in San Jose.
candidates.platform: Proposes immigration reform combining border enforcement with 'accountability and assimilation,' a simple low flat tax on wages, and water and energy projects including dam retrofits, hydropower, desalination and wildfire prevention for the Central Valley and Salinas Valley.

18.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings and a D+16 district; Lofgren won the primary 55%-29%.
18.partisan_lean: D+16 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 62.7%, Trump 34.2%
18.summary: Longtime Democrat Zoe Lofgren faces Republican Marine veteran Shane Lewis in a majority-Latino seat spanning eastern San Jose, Gilroy, Hollister, Salinas and Watsonville. Lewis's 29% primary share was the strongest Republican showing among the Bay Area seats, but the district remains safely Democratic. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+16 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Jimmy Panetta
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for the Central Coast, re-elected with 69.3% in 2024; former Monterey County prosecutor and U.S. Navy intelligence officer who served in Afghanistan.
candidates.platform: Priorities listed are reducing inflation through infrastructure and domestic manufacturing, environmental protection, housing affordability via grants and tax credits, expanding health care access and lowering drug prices, immigration reform paired with border security, and protecting voting rights and reproductive freedom. Endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

candidates.name: Peter Coe Verbica
candidates.bio: Managing director and Certified Financial Planner at Silicon Private Wealth and former adjunct economics professor at San Jose State; San Jose native with MIT and Santa Clara law degrees.
candidates.platform: Runs on affordability (lower state taxes, CEQA reform for housing, lower DMV fees, sound money), building the reservoirs voters approved, and a 'Bracero 2.0' legal-work immigration program for agriculture and tech. Endorsed by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC.

19.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings, D+18 PVI, and a 58%-20% primary.
19.partisan_lean: D+18 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 65.4%, Trump 31.0%
19.summary: Democrat Jimmy Panetta faces Republican financial planner Peter Verbica for the Central Coast seat covering Santa Cruz, Monterey, south San Jose and northern San Luis Obispo County. Every forecaster rates it Solid/Safe Democratic. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+18 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Vince Fong
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since winning the May 2024 special election to succeed Kevin McCarthy; former state assemblymember from Bakersfield.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on cutting taxes and regulations, affordability, energy independence, water and agriculture, aerospace and national defense, immigration and border security, support for law enforcement and Second Amendment protections. Endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

candidates.name: Sandra Van Scotter
candidates.bio: Community activist whose career has centered on advocacy for people unable to speak for themselves, including disability-benefit claimants.
candidates.platform: Supports Medicare for All as a single-payer transition, federal-state collaboration on agriculture, water and housing affordability, and streamlining access to veterans', Social Security and developmental disability benefits. Pledges participatory, constituent-driven representation.

20.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Republican ratings in California's most Republican district (R+16); Fong won the primary 68%-29%.
20.partisan_lean: R+16 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Trump 65.0%, Harris 32.8%
20.summary: Republican Vince Fong seeks a second full term against Democrat Sandra Van Scotter in the Kern/Tulare/Fresno County seat anchored in Bakersfield, Clovis and the southern Sierra. Proposition 50 left this district's conservative tilt intact or slightly stronger, as Republican-leaning Valley areas were consolidated here to make neighboring CA-22 and CA-21 more Democratic; it remains the state's most Republican seat.

candidates.name: Jim Costa
candidates.bio: Longtime Democratic U.S. Representative for the Fresno-based San Joaquin Valley seat, re-elected with 52.6% in 2024.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes Valley water supplies, jobs and economic development (citing the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act), federal funding for police, 911 staffing and anti-fentanyl efforts, expanded health care access, veterans, and reproductive freedom as a cosponsor of the Women's Health Protection Act. Endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and state Democratic leaders.

candidates.name: Kyle Kirkland
candidates.bio: Business owner and casino operator, president of the California Gaming Association and former Steinway Musical Instruments chairman; ran for CA-20 in 2024.
candidates.platform: Runs on lowering the cost of living through deregulation and spending cuts, government accountability, border security, support for law enforcement, water infrastructure for agriculture, and parent-focused education reform.

21.likely_winner_basis: Cook, Sabato and Inside Elections all rate the seat Likely Democratic (DDHQ Safe D); Costa led the primary 42%-26%, and Proposition 50 added about 2 points to the Democratic margin.
21.partisan_lean: D+5 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 51.6%, Trump 45.7%
21.summary: Democrat Jim Costa, who held on narrowly in 2024, faces Republican businessman Kyle Kirkland in the Fresno/Visalia seat. Proposition 50 added more of Fresno proper and Clovis while removing Republican-leaning towns such as Exeter, increasing the Democratic advantage by about 2.2 points; forecasters moved the race from competitive to Likely Democratic.

candidates.name: David Valadao
candidates.bio: Republican U.S. Representative (2013-2019 and since 2021) and Hanford-area dairy farmer; former state assemblymember.
candidates.platform: Campaigns as an independent-minded member focused on Central Valley water supply, agriculture, jobs, veterans and affordable health care, and says he has worked across the aisle on water infrastructure. Issue pages also call for a balanced budget, immigration reform, energy development and protecting Medicare and Social Security.

candidates.name: Randy Villegas
candidates.bio: Political science professor at College of the Sequoias, Visalia school board trustee and family auto-shop owner; son of immigrants and a Bakersfield native.
candidates.platform: Progressive economic populist backing Medicare for All, drug-price negotiation, the PRO Act, trade policy favoring Valley farmers over tariffs, and investment at home rather than in foreign wars. Pledges to refuse corporate PAC money, ban congressional stock trading and overturn Citizens United. Endorsed by Bernie Sanders, the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and later the DCCC and state party.

polls.pollster: Public Policy Polling (D), for ASPIRE PAC/SEIU (hypothetical: Valadao vs. generic Democrat)

22.likely_winner_basis: Toss-up: Cook and Inside Elections rate it Toss-up (Inside moved from Tilt R in September), Sabato Lean D and DDHQ Likely D; the only public head-to-head poll is a June campaign-sponsored survey showing Villegas +4, while Valadao led the primary 40.7%-32.4% and holds a large fundraising edge.
22.partisan_lean: D+1 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Trump 49.6%, Harris 47.7%
22.summary: One of the tightest House races in the state: Republican David Valadao, who has repeatedly survived in a Democratic-leaning Latino-majority Valley seat, faces Democrat Randy Villegas, who upset the DCCC-backed Assemblymember Jasmeet Bains in the primary. Proposition 50 explicitly targeted this seat, adding Democratic-leaning parts of Fresno and removing Republican-leaning areas of Hanford, Tulare and Porterville, shrinking Trump's 2024 margin from about 6 points to under 2.

candidates.name: Jay Obernolte
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2021 (CA-8 2021-2023, CA-23 since 2023) and video-game software entrepreneur; former state assemblymember and Big Bear Lake mayor.
candidates.platform: Priorities are cutting federal spending and inflation, tax relief for working families, securing the southern border, backing law enforcement against drug trafficking, veterans' benefits and full military funding. Endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

candidates.name: Tessa Lynn Hodge
candidates.bio: Licensed clinical social worker with nearly a decade of experience in foster care, school mental health and San Bernardino County policy; lifelong High Desert resident.
candidates.platform: Supports Medicare for All alongside expanding rural health services, living-wage jobs through investment, labor protections and workforce training, and affordable housing with renter protections. Favors term limits and frames her campaign as 'people over party.'

23.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Republican ratings, R+9 PVI, and a 57%-21% primary.
23.partisan_lean: R+9 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Trump 58.4%, Harris 39.0%
23.summary: Republican Jay Obernolte faces Democratic social worker Tessa Lynn Hodge in the High Desert/San Bernardino County seat (Victorville, Hesperia, Apple Valley, Barstow, Twentynine Palms). Proposition 50 left this district's conservative lean largely intact; it remains Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Salud Carbajal
candidates.bio: Democratic U.S. Representative for the Central Coast, re-elected with 62.7% in 2024.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on bringing both parties together on open-space preservation, infrastructure and broadband, clean energy, wildfire and drought response and health care access. Issue pages cover veterans, good-paying jobs, higher-education affordability, sensible gun laws, retirement security and reproductive rights.

candidates.name: Bob Smith
candidates.bio: Retired U.S. Navy commander and combat veteran with 26 years of service, now a senior engineering fellow for a defense contractor; Navy Engineer of the Year 2023.
candidates.platform: Stresses healing partisan division, restoring middle-class homeownership, 'peace through strength' military modernization, and attracting space, AI and fusion-energy jobs to the district. Supports term limits, four-year House terms and full federal spending transparency.

24.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings and a D+13 district; Carbajal won the primary 54%-36%.
24.partisan_lean: D+13 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 60.9%, Trump 36.0%
24.summary: Democrat Salud Carbajal faces Republican Navy veteran Bob Smith in the Santa Barbara/San Luis Obispo/Ventura coastal seat. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+13 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Raul Ruiz
candidates.bio: Democratic U.S. Representative and emergency physician who grew up in Coachella as the son of farmworkers; re-elected with 56.3% in 2024.
candidates.platform: Highlights protecting and expanding Social Security and Medicare, veterans' services and benefits, and small-business growth through reduced bureaucratic regulation, with additional issue positions on health care and the economy.

candidates.name: Joe Males
candidates.bio: Hemet city councilmember, U.S. Marine veteran and small-business owner.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes public safety and the rule of law, citing personal tragedy, along with infrastructure improvement, business growth and safer neighborhoods based on his council record.

25.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings and a 60%-19% primary, despite a modest D+4 PVI.
25.partisan_lean: D+4 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 51.8%, Trump 46.0%
25.summary: Democrat Raul Ruiz faces Republican Hemet councilmember Joe Males in the Imperial County/eastern Coachella Valley/Hemet seat. The district's presidential lean is modest, but Ruiz's 60% primary showing and unanimous Solid Democratic ratings make it uncompetitive. Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+4 under the new lines).

candidates.name: Jacqui Irwin
candidates.bio: California State Assemblymember for the 42nd district since 2014, engineer and former Thousand Oaks mayor.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on public safety, affordability and the needs of Ventura and Los Angeles counties while opposing the Trump administration's policies; cites a legislative record on homelessness, climate policy and gun safety. Endorsed by retiring Rep. Julia Brownley and Giffords.

candidates.name: Sam Gallucci
candidates.bio: Senior pastor of Embrace Church in Oxnard and former business and technology executive, including at IBM; ran in the 2021 gubernatorial recall.
candidates.platform: Supports lower taxes and deregulation to spur jobs, stricter immigration enforcement and opposition to sanctuary policies, and protecting life from conception. Opposes what he calls California's aggressive climate mandates such as the 2035 electric-vehicle requirement.

26.likely_winner_basis: Unanimous Solid/Safe Democratic ratings, a D+9 district, and a 41%-21% primary lead in a field where Democrats combined for about 60%.
26.partisan_lean: D+9 (Cook PVI, new lines); 2024 presidential in new district: Harris 56.2%, Trump 41.0%
26.summary: An open seat after Democrat Julia Brownley's retirement, pitting Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin against Republican pastor Sam Gallucci in the Ventura County seat (Oxnard, Camarillo, Thousand Oaks, Moorpark). Proposition 50 did not target this district; its lines were adjusted as part of the statewide redraw and its partisan character did not change materially (Cook PVI D+9 under the new lines).

candidates.name: George Whitesides
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative (since Jan. 2025) who flipped the seat in 2024; former NASA chief of staff and CEO of Virgin Galactic.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes lowering everyday costs and housing prices, defending Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid, and addressing the wildfire crisis. Also stresses local job creation, public safety funding and anti-corruption measures, and says he works across the aisle.

candidates.name: Jason Gibbs
candidates.bio: Santa Clarita city councilmember (elected 2020, mayor in 2023) and mechanical engineer who worked on rocket fueling infrastructure.
candidates.platform: Campaign centers on public safety, local control, job creation and lowering the cost of living. Presents himself as a problem-solver focused on strong families and protecting quality of life in the Santa Clarita Valley.

27.likely_winner_basis: All three major raters call the redrawn district Solid/Safe D and Harris carried it by about 10 points in 2024, despite Gibbs narrowly topping the June primary (41.0% to 40.6%) with the Democratic vote split among three candidates.
27.partisan_lean: D+6 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 53.4%, Trump 43.6% in the new district
27.summary: Freshman Democrat George Whitesides, who narrowly flipped this northern Los Angeles County seat in 2024, faces Santa Clarita councilmember Jason Gibbs. Proposition 50 made the district noticeably bluer: it added Democratic-leaning parts of the San Fernando Valley and dropped Republican-leaning Antelope Valley areas, increasing the Democratic advantage by roughly 5.5 points (from about Harris +4 to Harris +10), and raters moved it off the competitive list.

candidates.name: Judy Chu
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2009; member of the House Ways and Means Committee and chair emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus.
candidates.platform: Focuses on health care, Social Security and Medicare and family safety-net programs through her Ways and Means role. Advocates for Asian American and Pacific Islander communities and for copyright protections supporting the creative industries.

candidates.name: April Verlato
candidates.bio: Attorney and businesswoman; former Arcadia city councilmember (2016-2024) and mayor, and the 2024 Republican runner-up in this district.
candidates.platform: Platform stresses fiscal responsibility, support for law enforcement, national security and border security. Also calls for market-driven health care solutions, veterans' services and curbing inflation.

28.likely_winner_basis: Chu won 62.2% in the June primary against two opponents and all three raters list the seat as Solid/Safe D.
28.partisan_lean: D+14 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 61.0%, Trump 35.7% in the new district
28.summary: Longtime Democratic incumbent Judy Chu faces a rematch with Republican April Verlato in this San Gabriel Valley seat. The district's boundaries were adjusted under Proposition 50 but it remains a solidly Democratic area, and the general election is expected to be lopsided.

candidates.name: Luz Maria Rivas
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative (since Jan. 2025) and former California Assemblymember from the San Fernando Valley.
candidates.platform: Campaign cites opposition to Trump administration health care cuts, oversight of ICE detention and a call to abolish ICE, and securing federal funds for higher education, infrastructure and public housing in the Valley. Also stresses environmental protection and her backing from labor unions and teachers.

candidates.name: Angélica María Dueñas
candidates.bio: Human-resources professional and former president of the Sun Valley Neighborhood Council; runner-up in this district in 2020 and 2022 and candidate in 2018 and 2024.
candidates.platform: Progressive platform calling for abolishing ICE, housing as a right with anti-gentrification measures, universal health care and clean energy. Refuses corporate PAC, AIPAC, crypto and AI-industry money and opposes U.S. funding for Israel's military operations in Gaza.

29.likely_winner_basis: Rivas took 51.0% in the primary, more than double Dueñas's 24.9%, in a Democrat-vs-Democrat general where the Republican vote (24%) is now up for grabs.
29.partisan_lean: D+19 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 65.3%, Trump 31.6% in the new district
29.summary: This San Fernando Valley seat features an all-Democratic general election between incumbent Luz Rivas and repeat challenger Angélica María Dueñas after the lone Republican finished a close third in the primary. Proposition 50 adjusted the district's lines but left it one of the most Democratic seats in the region; the outcome is a question of which Democrat wins rather than party control.

candidates.name: Laura Friedman
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative (since Jan. 2025); former California Assemblymember and Glendale city councilmember and mayor.
candidates.platform: Priorities are affordable housing production and homelessness, fighting climate change with 100% clean energy and transit investment, and protecting civil rights including abortion access and voting rights. Cites a record of passing environmental and housing legislation in Sacramento.

candidates.name: Scott Meyers
candidates.bio: Attorney running as a Republican in the Burbank-Glendale-Hollywood area.
candidates.platform: Calls for federal accountability over how California state and local governments spend tax money and for investigating fraud and waste. Pledges to restrict transgender athletes from girls' sports, bring film and television production back to the district, and hold regular open press conferences.

30.likely_winner_basis: Friedman won an outright majority (52.7%) in a seven-candidate primary while Meyers took 16.6%; all raters have the seat Solid/Safe D.
30.partisan_lean: D+21 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 68.3%, Trump 28.3% in the new district
30.summary: Freshman Democrat Laura Friedman is heavily favored over Republican attorney Scott Meyers in this district covering Burbank, Glendale and parts of the eastern San Fernando Valley and Hollywood Hills. Proposition 50 altered the district's edges but it remains one of the most Democratic seats in Los Angeles County.

candidates.name: Gil Cisneros
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since Jan. 2025 (also served 2019-2021); Navy veteran and former Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness.
candidates.platform: Platform stresses anti-corruption and campaign-finance reform, refusing donations from pharmaceutical, oil, tobacco, gun and private-prison interests. Also prioritizes raising wages, lowering prescription drug and housing costs, reproductive rights, and services for veterans and students.

candidates.name: Eric Ching
candidates.bio: Former Walnut city councilmember (2012-2024) and two-time mayor; Republican runner-up in the 38th district in 2022 and 2024.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes community safety, the economy and foreign relations, along with parental rights and a focus on STEM in schools. Pledges to cut government fraud and waste and says he will defend the Constitution and put faith and people's interests first.

31.likely_winner_basis: Cisneros took 61.1% in the primary against two Republicans who combined for 39%, and the seat is rated Solid/Safe D by all three outlets.
31.partisan_lean: D+8 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 54.6%, Trump 42.4% in the new district
31.summary: Democrat Gil Cisneros seeks a second consecutive term against Republican Eric Ching in this eastern San Gabriel Valley seat. Proposition 50 redrew the district's boundaries (Ching previously ran in the neighboring 38th), but it remains a Democratic-leaning area where Harris won by about 12 points in 2024.

candidates.name: Brad Sherman
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 1997; senior member of the House Foreign Affairs and Financial Services committees.
candidates.platform: Runs on consumer protection (he helped create the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau), transit and freeway funding including Sepulveda Pass rail, and preservation of the Santa Monica Mountains. Highlights Palisades fire recovery and his early opposition to Donald Trump, including introducing impeachment articles in 2017.

candidates.name: Larry Thompson
candidates.bio: Talent manager, film producer and lawyer; U.S. Army Reserve veteran and the 2024 Republican runner-up in this district.
candidates.platform: Describes himself as a moderate Republican focused on rebuilding communities hit by the 2025 fires and finding common ground across party lines. Pledges to represent constituents over party leadership and to reduce partisan labeling.

32.likely_winner_basis: Although Sherman led the primary with only 36.8% to Thompson's 32.7%, Democrats combined for over 66% of the primary vote in a D+14 district and all raters list it Solid/Safe D.
32.partisan_lean: D+14 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 61.0%, Trump 36.0% in the new district
32.summary: Veteran Democrat Brad Sherman faces a rematch with Republican Larry Thompson in this West San Fernando Valley and Westside seat, where a crowded field of Democratic challengers held Sherman to 37% in the primary. Proposition 50 modified the district's lines but it remains strongly Democratic, and the consolidated Democratic vote makes Sherman the heavy favorite.

candidates.name: Pete Aguilar
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2015 and chair of the House Democratic Caucus; former mayor of Redlands.
candidates.platform: Emphasizes lowering prescription drug and housing costs, expanding American manufacturing and protecting health care, Social Security and veterans' programs from cuts. Says he works across the aisle on veterans' issues, small-business tax relief and immigration reform.

candidates.name: Stephanie Vargas
candidates.bio: Former Chief Deputy City Clerk of Colton (2024-2026).
candidates.platform: Priorities are public safety and support for police and firefighters, parental rights, and lowering the cost of living. Calls for addressing the housing crisis and delivering tax relief for families and businesses.

33.likely_winner_basis: Aguilar won 53.5% in a seven-way primary (Vargas 17.5%) and all three raters list the San Bernardino-based seat Solid/Safe D.
33.partisan_lean: D+7 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 53.4%, Trump 43.7% in the new district
33.summary: House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar is favored over Republican Stephanie Vargas in this San Bernardino-centered Inland Empire seat. Proposition 50 redrew the district's boundaries for the 2026 cycle, but it remains a Democratic-leaning district that Harris carried by nearly 10 points.

candidates.name: Jimmy Gomez
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2017; former California Assemblymember and political director for the United Nurses Associations of California.
candidates.platform: Cosponsor of Medicare for All and the Green New Deal and a member of the Progressive Caucus; emphasizes affordable housing, senior housing, protecting Medicare, Social Security, Medicaid and SNAP, and addressing grocery and childcare costs. Highlights immigration oversight of ICE facilities and a lawsuit over access, and criminal-justice reform.

candidates.name: Angela Gonzales-Torres
candidates.bio: Academic counselor at Pasadena City College and affordable-housing program director; former president of the Historic Highland Park Neighborhood Council.
candidates.platform: Democratic socialist backed by Justice Democrats and LA DSA running on affordability, ending ICE and for-profit prisons, expanded housing vouchers and rent relief, and funding education and youth programs. Attacks Gomez over corporate PAC, crypto and AIPAC money, opposes U.S. military aid to Israel, and has called on him to resign over the ethics inquiry.

polls.pollster: Center for Strategic Politics (sponsored by Gonzales-Torres campaign)
Upswing Research & Strategy (D; sponsored by Guardrails Alliance)

34.likely_winner_basis: Gomez led the primary 46.0% to 30.7%, but the only two public polls (both sponsored by Gonzales-Torres or allied groups) show the challenger ahead by 3 and 10 points, so the outcome is uncertain.
34.summary: This downtown and eastside Los Angeles seat is an all-Democratic contest between incumbent Jimmy Gomez and challenger Angela Gonzales-Torres, who has consolidated support from Justice Democrats, DSA and the Working Families Party. In August 2026 the House Ethics Committee opened an inquiry into allegations against Gomez, which he denies (Semafor, Sept. 10, 2026). The district's boundaries are unchanged under Proposition 50, so the seat stays safely Democratic regardless of which candidate wins.

candidates.name: Norma Torres
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2015; former Pomona mayor, state legislator and 911 emergency dispatcher.
candidates.platform: Campaign emphasizes safer communities, lowering costs, stronger schools and good jobs for Inland Empire working families. Pledges to defend constituents from the Trump administration's immigration enforcement and from cuts to health care and education.

candidates.name: Mike Cargile
candidates.bio: Independent filmmaker and president of Big Event Pictures; U.S. Army veteran and the Republican runner-up in this district in 2020, 2022 and 2024.
candidates.platform: Platform centers on border security, which he frames as stopping an invasion, fentanyl and human trafficking. Opposes transgender participation in girls' sports and what he calls the sexualization of children, and pledges to protect gas stoves and cars, food prices and energy independence.

35.likely_winner_basis: Torres beat Cargile 59.5%-40.4% in a two-way primary, matching their prior matchups, and the seat is rated Solid/Safe D.
35.partisan_lean: D+6 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 52.4%, Trump 44.6% in the new district
35.summary: Democrat Norma Torres faces Republican Mike Cargile for the fourth consecutive cycle in this Inland Empire seat. Under Proposition 50 the district now includes Pomona, Ontario, Chino, Chino Hills, Rancho Cucamonga, Fontana, Upland, Claremont, Montclair, Corona, Norco, Eastvale and Bloomington; Harris carried the new lines by about 8 points.

candidates.name: Ted Lieu
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2015 and vice chair of the House Democratic Caucus; Air Force veteran serving on the Foreign Affairs and Judiciary committees.
candidates.platform: Frames his campaign around defending democracy and the rule of law against extremism and corruption, with a focus on oversight of the Trump administration. Highlights veterans' issues including $35 million for the West LA VA and housing for homeless veterans.

candidates.name: Houston Brignano
candidates.bio: Technology executive and Marine Corps veteran who served in Iraq.
candidates.platform: Calls for radical fiscal transparency, publishing all meetings, donors and vote explanations, and refuses corporate PAC money. Proposes innovation zones and deregulation to spur tech, manufacturing and energy jobs and lower housing costs, plus portable health savings accounts and price transparency in health care.

36.likely_winner_basis: Lieu won 60.9% in a seven-candidate primary (Brignano 15.3%) in a D+21 district rated Solid/Safe D.
36.summary: Democrat Ted Lieu is heavily favored over Republican Houston Brignano in this coastal Westside and South Bay seat. The district's boundaries are unchanged under Proposition 50, and it remains one of the most Democratic districts in Southern California.

candidates.name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2023; former state senator and Assemblymember and former Los Angeles Community College District trustee.
candidates.platform: Campaign emphasizes job creation and economic opportunity in underserved communities, affordable higher education and career training, and access to quality childcare and early education. Draws on a background in arts-based community rebuilding and advocacy for working families.

candidates.name: Samantha Mota
candidates.bio: Community activist running a self-described grassroots campaign.
candidates.platform: Says she is passionate about immigration reform, universal health care, paid family leave and economic stability. Pitches herself as a transparent, bold alternative focused on increasing participation and reducing corruption and abuse of power.

37.likely_winner_basis: Kamlager-Dove took 55.2% in a nine-candidate primary versus 11.7% for Mota, who edged out the top Republican for second place.
37.summary: Incumbent Democrat Sydney Kamlager-Dove faces fellow Democrat Samantha Mota in this South and Central Los Angeles seat after Mota narrowly beat Republican Baltazar Fedalizo for the second general-election slot. The district's boundaries are unchanged under Proposition 50 and it is one of the most Democratic districts in the state; the incumbent is a prohibitive favorite.

incumbent.name: Linda Sánchez
incumbent.note: running in CA-41 (seat left open by redistricting)

candidates.name: Hilda Solis
candidates.bio: Los Angeles County Supervisor (2014-present), former U.S. Secretary of Labor (2009-2013) and former U.S. Representative (2001-2009).
candidates.platform: Says she is running to make government work for people rather than the powerful, with priorities of affordable housing, accessible health care and mental health services, and transparency in government. Supports bold climate action including clean-energy and electric-vehicle incentives and programs to build trust between communities and law enforcement.

candidates.name: Pedro Casas
candidates.bio: Psychologist (also known as Antonio Casas) who ran for the 31st district in 2024.
candidates.platform: Platform stresses securing the southern border and immigration reforms prioritizing national security, tougher criminal-justice policies and public safety. Calls for tax cuts and deregulation to fight inflation and reduce housing and living costs, and opposes transgender athletes competing in women's sports.

38.likely_winner_basis: Solis led the primary 47.6% to 35.8% with Democrats combining for roughly 64%, and all raters list the open seat Solid/Safe D (a Democratic hold).
38.partisan_lean: D+8 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 54.5%, Trump 42.2% in the new district
38.summary: This southeast Los Angeles County seat is open because Proposition 50 reshaped the region and incumbent Linda Sánchez chose to run in the redrawn 41st district instead. The new 38th takes in communities such as Baldwin Park, El Monte, Bell, Cudahy, Commerce and Diamond Bar; former Labor Secretary and county supervisor Hilda Solis is favored over Republican psychologist Pedro Casas.

candidates.name: Mark Takano
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2013 and ranking member of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee; former public school teacher and Riverside Community College trustee.
candidates.platform: Focuses on veterans' services, public and higher education and workforce training. Emphasizes his record on the Veterans' Affairs and Education and Workforce committees and his roots in Riverside.

candidates.name: Steve Manos
candidates.bio: Lake Elsinore city councilmember; chair of the Southwest Riverside Energy Authority and former Riverside Transit Authority director.
candidates.platform: Runs on faith, family and affordability, pledging to remove regulatory barriers that raise housing and basic-needs costs and to curb hedge-fund purchases of homes. Also prioritizes parental rights, national security and funding I-215 freeway repairs and transit capacity.

39.likely_winner_basis: Takano beat Manos 61.0%-39.0% in a two-candidate primary and the Riverside-based seat is rated Solid/Safe D.
39.partisan_lean: D+7 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 53.2%, Trump 43.7% in the new district
39.summary: Democrat Mark Takano faces Republican Lake Elsinore councilmember Steve Manos in this western Riverside County seat covering Riverside, Moreno Valley, Jurupa Valley and Perris. Proposition 50 redrew the district's boundaries for 2026 but it remains Democratic-leaning, with Harris winning the new lines by about 9.5 points.

incumbent.name: Young Kim
incumbent.note: running here; Ken Calvert (R, incumbent of the old CA-41) was drawn into this district and is also running here

candidates.name: Ken Calvert
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 1993 (currently for the old CA-41, Riverside County), a former restaurant and real-estate small-business owner and senior House appropriator.
candidates.platform: Runs on his record and seniority, citing authorship of the E-Verify law and more than a billion dollars in federal funding secured for Riverside County transportation, water and clean-air projects. Pledges to back President Trump's agenda of lower taxes, border security, lower housing costs and safer streets, and argues he already represents the majority of the new district.

candidates.name: Young Kim
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2021 (CA-40, previously CA-39), a former state assemblymember, business owner, financial analyst and longtime aide to Rep. Ed Royce.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on lowering the cost of gas, groceries, utilities, health care and prescription drugs, and on fighting waste and fraud (citing her No More Scams Act). Supports congressional term limits and a ban on members trading individual stocks, and describes herself as an 'America First' ally of President Trump on border security, crime and spending.

polls.pollster: Grassroots Targeting (sponsored by California First Fund, pro-Kim)

40.likely_winner_basis: Republican hold is certain, but the member-vs-member outcome is unclear: Calvert won the primary 35%-21% and represents 51% of the new district, while the only public general-election polls (all Kim-aligned) show a tie or a Kim lead, with Democratic voters (43% of the primary vote) deciding.
40.summary: Prop 50 shed much of the old 40th's Orange County territory and added heavily Republican parts of Riverside County from the old 41st and 48th, making the seat about 10 points more Republican and packing two GOP incumbents, Ken Calvert and Young Kim, into one district. Both advanced from the top-two primary, so the November race is an intra-party contest in which both candidates have emphasized their support for President Trump; it is the only member-vs-member House general election in California.

incumbent.name: Linda Sánchez
incumbent.note: running here; previously represented the old CA-38

candidates.name: Linda Sánchez
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2003, a UC Berkeley and UCLA Law graduate who worked as a labor and employment attorney and led the Orange County Central Labor Council.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on lowering prices for groceries, utilities and child care and on protecting working families, citing legislation she passed on insurance pricing equity. Opposes the Trump administration's immigration enforcement, saying she pushed to remove DHS Secretary Kristi Noem and to stop funding ICE raids.

candidates.name: Mitch Clemmons
candidates.bio: Plumbing contractor and small-business owner since 2002, a former warehouse manager who studied aerospace engineering technology at Cal Poly Pomona and was the 2022 Republican nominee for state Senate District 30.
candidates.platform: Prioritizes election integrity, restoring 'law and order' with accountability for minor crimes and a humane but firm approach to homelessness, and ending what he calls taxpayer-funded fraud through NGOs. Emphasizes parents' rights and schools that teach core skills rather than 'political indoctrination.'

41.likely_winner_basis: All major forecasters rate the seat Solid/Safe Democratic in a D+9 district; Democrats combined for about 64% of the primary vote.
41.summary: Prop 50 dismantled Ken Calvert's Riverside County-based 41st and rebuilt the district number in Democratic-leaning eastern Los Angeles County and northern Orange County, turning a Lean Republican seat into what Inside Elections called a near-automatic Democratic pickup. Longtime Rep. Linda Sánchez moved over from the old 38th and faces Republican plumbing contractor Mitch Clemmons, who finished a close second in the primary while three Democrats split the rest of the vote.

candidates.name: Robert Garcia
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2023 and ranking member of the House Oversight Committee, a Peruvian-born former mayor of Long Beach (2014-2022) and university lecturer.
candidates.platform: Frames the race around defending democracy from the 'extreme far-right' and holding the Trump administration accountable. Supports Medicare for All, clean-energy jobs, higher wages, affordable housing, union protections, gun-violence prevention and student-debt cancellation.

candidates.name: Brian Burley
candidates.bio: Huntington Beach City School District trustee elected in 2024, an IT consulting business owner and USC public-policy graduate who has run for Congress several times before.
candidates.platform: Pitches 'servant leadership' over partisanship, citing his school-board record on parents' voices and fiscal stewardship. Priorities are safe neighborhoods, quality education, lower costs and an economy that lets families get ahead.

42.likely_winner_basis: Garcia took 56.5% in the primary against a split Republican field and every forecaster rates the seat Solid/Safe Democratic.
42.summary: The Long Beach-based 42nd was one of the districts Prop 50 made much less Democratic (its Democratic registration edge fell by roughly 19 points) as Republican-leaning coastal Orange County areas such as Huntington Beach were added to absorb GOP voters from neighboring seats. It nonetheless remains comfortably Democratic, and Rep. Robert Garcia faces Republican school-board trustee Brian Burley.

candidates.name: Maxine Waters
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 1991 and senior Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, a former Head Start teacher who served in the California Assembly from 1977 to 1991.
candidates.platform: Her official issue priorities center on housing and homelessness, consumer and financial protection, health care, education, criminal-justice reform, immigration and diversity and inclusion. She is a prominent critic of the Trump administration and runs on her long record of delivering federal resources to South Los Angeles communities.

candidates.name: Cristian Morales
candidates.bio: Guatemalan-born manufacturing executive with more than 20 years in the automotive, aerospace and defense industries and degrees from Cornell and Purdue.
candidates.platform: Campaigns under the slogan 'For All Voices' on restoring civil dialogue across differences, limited but accountable government, border security, public safety and economic opportunity for working families. Calls for a Reagan-style Republican outreach to Latino communities and a 'fresh perspective' after one-party rule in California.

43.likely_winner_basis: Waters won nearly 64% of the primary vote in a D+27 district rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster.
43.summary: The South Los Angeles-based 43rd (Compton, Watts, Inglewood, Hawthorne, Gardena, Torrance) saw only modest boundary changes under Prop 50 and remains one of the most Democratic districts in the country. Longtime Rep. Maxine Waters faces Republican manufacturing executive Cristian Morales, who edged a Democratic challenger for the second top-two slot.

candidates.name: Nanette Barragán
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2017 and a member of the Energy and Commerce Committee, a UCLA and USC Law graduate who previously served on the Hermosa Beach City Council.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on protecting and expanding Medicare and Social Security, raising the minimum wage and bringing good-paying jobs to the harbor-area district. Emphasizes affordable college and early-childhood education, immigrant rights, environmental justice and clean-energy transition for communities affected by port and refinery pollution.

candidates.name: Genevieve Angel
candidates.bio: Family nurse practitioner, health-care executive and small-business owner who describes herself as a Filipina-Latin American mother who has lived in the district for nearly 30 years.
candidates.platform: Runs as a non-politician focused on fiscal responsibility, public safety, health-care reform and 'educational freedom.' Says families in the district are being squeezed by costs and that the American Dream is slipping away for the next generation.

44.likely_winner_basis: Barragán won 77% of the primary vote in a two-candidate field in a D+20 district rated Solid/Safe Democratic.
44.summary: The 44th, running from South Gate and Compton down to the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, was little changed by Prop 50 and remains heavily Democratic. Rep. Nanette Barragán faces Republican nurse practitioner Genevieve Angel in a rematch of the two-person primary.

candidates.name: Derek Tran
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative elected in 2024 by flipping the seat, a consumer-rights attorney, policy analyst and eight-year U.S. Army Reserve veteran.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on lowering prescription-drug and health-care costs, protecting abortion rights and holding corporations accountable for rising prices. Stresses a bipartisan, 'people over politics' approach drawn from his military service and pledges to protect democracy and civil liberties.

candidates.name: Chuong Vo
candidates.bio: Retired 26-year Torrance Police Department officer who served on the Cerritos City Council (2020-2025), including as mayor.
candidates.platform: Says government's first job is keeping families safe and pledges to back law enforcement, lower costs and hold all levels of government accountable. Calls federal deficits a spending problem rather than a revenue problem and says he will not simply vote along party lines.

45.likely_winner_basis: All three major forecasters moved the race to Likely Democratic by October 2026; Tran took 53.8% in the primary against a five-way Republican field and had raised roughly ten times as much as Vo by mid-year.
45.summary: Prop 50 nudged the Little Saigon-centered 45th a few points toward Democrats by adding parts of Norwalk and Santa Ana and dropping Brea and Placentia, taking it from roughly D+1 to about D+4-5 on 2024 presidential numbers. Freshman Rep. Derek Tran, who won by a few hundred votes in 2024, now faces former Cerritos mayor and retired police officer Chuong Vo in a race forecasters have steadily downgraded from Toss-up to Likely Democratic.

candidates.name: Lou Correa
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2017, a former state assemblymember, state senator and Orange County supervisor with an MBA and law degree from UCLA.
candidates.platform: Presents himself as a pragmatic, bipartisan problem-solver focused on helping working-class Orange County families reach the middle class. Highlights support for veterans, Dreamers and immigrant communities in Anaheim, Santa Ana, Orange and Garden Grove, and on delivering federal resources locally.

candidates.name: David Pan
candidates.bio: UC Irvine professor of German since 2006 and former McKinsey consultant, with degrees from Stanford and Columbia, who was the 2024 Republican nominee in this district.
candidates.platform: Proposes phasing out federal welfare and entitlement programs and returning the money to taxpayers, with a new system to guarantee Social Security for those 37 and older. Also backs school choice and vouchers, more police, border security, lower taxes and regulation on small business, and health-care price transparency with high-deductible plans.

46.likely_winner_basis: Correa won a majority in the primary and the D+10 seat is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster.
46.summary: The central Orange County 46th (Anaheim, Santa Ana, Orange, Garden Grove) changed little under Prop 50 and remains a solidly Democratic, heavily Latino seat. Rep. Lou Correa faces a rematch with UC Irvine professor David Pan, whom he defeated 63%-37% in 2024.

candidates.name: Dave Min
candidates.bio: First-term U.S. Representative elected in 2024, a former state senator, UC Irvine law professor and SEC enforcement attorney with degrees from Wharton and Harvard Law.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on holding the Trump administration accountable, including calls to impeach cabinet officials and his Oversight Committee work on the Epstein files, and on opposing ICE enforcement tactics. Also runs on anti-corruption measures, workforce housing, reproductive rights, gun safety and economic policies for working families.

candidates.name: Jenny Rae Le Roux
candidates.bio: Entrepreneur and managing director of the consulting-prep firm Management Consulted, a 2022 Republican candidate for governor who has led a 'California DOGE' effort auditing state spending.
candidates.platform: Focuses on cutting government waste, fraud and mismanagement to lower the cost of housing, gas and groceries, drawing on her 'CAL DOGE' reviews of state spending. Promises to bring private-sector discipline to Washington.

47.likely_winner_basis: Prop 50 moved the seat from roughly D+4 to D+10 and all forecasters now rate it Solid/Safe Democratic; Min led the primary by about 20 points.
47.summary: Prop 50 reshaped the coastal Orange County 47th, removing Republican-leaning Huntington Beach and most of Newport Beach and adding Tustin, Aliso Viejo, Lake Forest and other south-county cities, so that about 60% of the district is new to Rep. Dave Min. The change turned one of 2024's closest races into a seat forecasters rate safely Democratic; Min faces Republican entrepreneur Jenny Rae Le Roux.

candidates.name: Marni von Wilpert
candidates.bio: San Diego City Council member since 2020 (District 5), a Fordham-trained attorney who worked for the Economic Policy Institute and the City of San Diego.
candidates.platform: Campaigns as a check on President Trump, opposing ICE raids and tariffs and pledging to restore Affordable Care Act tax credits and add a public option. Promises to cut red tape to build more affordable housing and lower costs for families.

candidates.name: Jim Desmond
candidates.bio: San Diego County Supervisor since 2019 (District 5) and 12-year former mayor of San Marcos, a U.S. Navy veteran and retired Delta Air Lines captain.
candidates.platform: Runs on making California affordable through lower taxes, less regulation and lower energy and insurance costs, and on 'treatment-first' homelessness policy tied to measurable results. Supports a secure border paired with a functioning legal immigration system, and stresses his record of local, bipartisan governance.

polls.pollster: Lake Research Partners (D, von Wilpert campaign)
