48.likely_winner_basis: Forecasters rate the open seat Lean/Tilt Democratic and the latest independent poll (SurveyUSA, Oct 1-7) has von Wilpert ahead 47-38, though Desmond topped the fragmented primary with 39% and Democrats combined for only 51%.
48.partisan_lean: D+2 (Cook PVI); 2024 presidential: Harris 50.4%, Trump 47.0% (old district: Trump 56%, Harris 41%)
48.summary: Prop 50 transformed Darrell Issa's safely Republican 48th by removing the Temecula Valley and most of east San Diego County and adding Democratic-leaning Palm Springs and the Coachella Valley plus north San Diego County cities such as Vista and San Marcos, an 18-point swing toward Democrats on 2024 presidential results. With Issa retiring, San Diego County Supervisor Jim Desmond (R) and San Diego City Councilmember Marni von Wilpert (D) advanced from a 12-candidate primary in one of the most closely followed House races in the country.

candidates.name: Mike Levin
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2019, a Stanford and Duke Law graduate who worked as an environmental and energy regulatory attorney.
candidates.platform: Runs on a record of bipartisan lawmaking and more than $1.1 billion in federal funding secured for the district, with emphasis on veterans (named VFW Legislator of the Year), clean water, infrastructure and coastal and environmental protection. Pitches himself as putting 'people ahead of politics.'

candidates.name: Armen Kurdian
candidates.bio: Retired U.S. Navy captain with 25 years of service (1993-2018) and an engineering manager, with graduate degrees from the Naval Postgraduate School and Cornell.
candidates.platform: Makes reducing the cost of living his top priority and blames Sacramento policies for job losses and out-migration. Calls for schools to focus on core academics and trades, and for working with business and labor to bring manufacturing and shipbuilding back to California.

49.likely_winner_basis: Levin won nearly 56% of the primary and every forecaster rates the redrawn D+7 seat Solid/Safe Democratic.
49.summary: Prop 50 made the north San Diego County coastal 49th about four points more Democratic by adding parts of the city of San Diego and dropping Republican-leaning south Orange County cities such as Dana Point, though it keeps San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano. Rep. Mike Levin, who won by about four points in 2024, faces retired Navy captain Armen Kurdian in a race now rated safely Democratic.

candidates.name: Scott Peters
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2013 (CA-50 since 2023, previously CA-52), an environmental attorney who was San Diego's first City Council president and chaired the Port of San Diego.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on making San Diego affordable through lower housing costs and utility bills, protecting Medicare and lowering health-care costs, and investing in clean energy and infrastructure. Highlights more than $650 million he secured to fix the South Bay sewage plant and a record of bipartisan legislation.

candidates.name: Steve Cohen
candidates.bio: Broadcast journalist of roughly 50 years who spent more than two decades as news director of San Diego's KUSI-TV.
candidates.platform: Runs as a non-politician on a 'San Diego Affordability Agenda' addressing housing supply, grocery and health-care costs, benefits for seniors and veterans, federal spending and border security. Argues the incumbent has had more than a decade in Washington while these problems worsened.

50.likely_winner_basis: Peters led the primary by eight points and the D+10 district is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster, though it became less Democratic under Prop 50.
50.summary: The 50th (coastal and central San Diego, Coronado, Poway, Escondido) was one of the districts Prop 50 made less Democratic, absorbing Republican-leaning areas from Darrell Issa's old 48th and cutting its Democratic registration edge by roughly 12 points, but it remains solidly blue. Rep. Scott Peters faces former KUSI news director Steve Cohen, who consolidated the Republican vote in the primary.

candidates.name: Sara Jacobs
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2021, a third-generation San Diegan and Columbia graduate who worked at the State Department, UNICEF and the UN and founded San Diego for Every Child.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on treating health care as a human right, affordable housing, bold action on climate change and ending gun violence. Emphasizes defending access to reproductive care and equal opportunity for every child.

candidates.name: Ricardo Cabrera
candidates.bio: San Diego small-business owner and cybersecurity professional.
candidates.platform: Supports congressional term limits and 'citizen legislators,' fiscal responsibility and public safety. Says families are being priced out of California and promises to prioritize affordability and results over bureaucracy.

51.likely_winner_basis: Jacobs won nearly 58% of the primary in a D+10 seat rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster.
51.summary: The San Diego-centered 51st took in some Republican-leaning inland territory under Prop 50 as GOP voters from the old 48th were distributed among the San Diego districts, but it remains comfortably Democratic. Rep. Sara Jacobs faces Republican cybersecurity professional Ricardo Cabrera.

candidates.name: Juan Vargas
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative since 2013 and a member of the Financial Services Committee, a National City native and Harvard Law graduate who served in the state Assembly and Senate.
candidates.platform: Runs on his legislative record, including bills on medical-supply production, anti-trafficking and corporate ESG disclosure, and on preserving landmarks such as Chicano Park. Emphasizes opportunity for immigrant and border communities and ensuring 'no one is left behind' in the South Bay.

candidates.name: Jeff Belle
candidates.bio: Business owner who cites federal and local government experience and describes himself as a supporter of President Trump.
candidates.platform: Prioritizes affordability through more housing supply, deregulation, tax restraint and tax relief for veterans and seniors, plus federal funding to address the Tijuana River sewage crisis. Backs secure borders combined with faster legal immigration and an earned legal status for long-term undocumented residents who contribute, and an SBA overhaul.

52.likely_winner_basis: Vargas won 56.5% of the primary and the D+11 border district is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by every forecaster.
52.summary: The 52nd, covering Chula Vista, National City, Imperial Beach and the border communities of south San Diego County, absorbed some Republican-leaning east-county territory under Prop 50 but stays solidly Democratic. Rep. Juan Vargas faces Republican business owner Jeff Belle.
